newsitem.title: USA: E.Caribbean key to U.S. drug trade - report.
newsitem.headline: E.Caribbean key to U.S. drug trade - report.

text.p: The islands of the eastern Caribbean are once again a key transit zone for cocaine and heroin heading to the United States, The Washington Post reported Monday, quoting law enforcement officials.

The newspaper said drug trafficking was on the upswing again in the region in recent months, after slacking off for nearly a decade, and analysts feared it could pose a potential threat to the region's fragile and ill-equipped governments.

Felix Jiminez, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration's special agent in charge of the Caribbean described Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory in the Caribbean, as an "island under siege", noting that drugs could be shipped from the island anywhere in the United States without passing through customs.
He said the island was "the epicentre of the Caribbean drugs en route to the U.S. mainland, Europe and Canada."

"The Caribbean is a significant drug transit zone because there are lots of harbours, lots of airstrips and governments without a lot of money," the newspaper quoted Jonathan Winter, deputy assistant secretary of state for law enforcement and crime as saying.
Winter said the matter was "of real concern to the United States and Caribbean nations."

Another State Department official, Jane Becker, warned in an Aug. 27 declassified report that "drug traffickers have penetrated the highest levels of society and government institutions in Antigua, Trinidad and Tobago, St. Kitts and Neves, Aruba, Jamaica and the Dominican Republic," the paper reported.
Drug smugglers have turned to the Caribbean again as law enforcement efforts have been increased in Mexico, another key transit site for drugs headed to the United States.

Some Caribbean countries, where offshore banking is protected by strict confidentiality laws, are also attracting hundreds of millions of dollars of drug money that is laundered through local banks, one United Nations official told the paper.
